snapshot_auto.quote: pause / resume / snapshots / fork (a sandbox is a claimed Pod, not a microVM, so there is no memory image)
snapshot_auto.note: E2B autoPause/autoResume are refused at create (HTTP 400). On idle timeout or kill the Pod is restarted onto the idle image and returned to the pool; state is discarded.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: pause / resume / snapshots / fork (a sandbox is a claimed Pod, not a microVM, so there is no memory image)
snapshot_on_demand.note: Listed under 'Not supported (HTTP 501)', category architectural. Templates are container images you build in your own CI; no snapshot format.

harness_api.quote: The brain keeps running wherever you run it; the hands become a sandbox bound to the conversation.
harness_api.note: The first-party agent integration ('Brain and Hands', @scitix/agentbox-hands for Claude Agent SDK, OpenCode, generic MCP) is the inverse model: the harness runs outside and only its bash/read/write/edit/grep/glob/apply_patch tools act on the sandbox. No API to start/stream/resume a harness inside the sandbox; the console assistant also runs its brain outside. Agent skills (abx-*) for Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode drive the platform, not an in-sandbox harness.

egress_allowlist.quote: Naming an allow list is what makes everything else a deny — the entries are the whole of what is reachable. A CIDR or a bare IP works in the same list.
egress_allowlist.note: Per-sandbox rules on create (E2B network.allow_out / deny_out, allow_internet_access=False), live replacement via PUT /sandboxes/{id}/network. Enforced by an egress-proxy sidecar plus an iptables nat redirect installed by a CAP_NET_ADMIN init container in the Pod netns (not in the sandbox image). Requires the env's gateway switch (overrides.gateway.enabled); otherwise rule-bearing creates are refused 400. Hostnames matched on HTTP Host (:80) / TLS SNI (:443) only; other ports CIDR-only. Metadata/link-local always denied; RFC1918 denied by default. Self-hosted: the operator runs it.

egress_http_rules.quote: `HTTP` rules match on the `Host` header, `TLS` rules on the SNI.
egress_http_rules.note: network.rules are per-host header transforms (credential injection), not method/path filters: the injection rule type holds only Host + Headers (handlers/egress.go). No method/path/header allow/deny rules documented.

ingress_rules.note: Sandbox ports are reached through the Envoy data plane (/sandboxes/<id>/<port>/... or x-sandbox-id/x-sandbox-port headers) and the ExtProc validates an API key on every inbound request. Self-hosted: the operator also decides whether/how the ingress is published (Helm ingress.host). No per-port public/private toggle or IP allowlist documented.

secret_proxy.quote: The value never enters the sandbox. The sandbox holds a **decoy** — a placeholder that looks like a token — and the egress sidecar substitutes the real one as the request leaves, for the hosts and headers the rule names.
secret_proxy.note: Write-only vault (E2B Secret API) + per-sandbox network.rules header transforms for any named host (no wildcards); TLS MITM with a per-sandbox CA installed in the trust store. HTTP/HTTPS on ports 80/443 only; header rewrite only (no body/query); no non-HTTP protocols (DB, SSH). Requires the env's egress gateway.

volume_attach.note: Env-level only (overrides.volumes on the SandboxEnv, Kubernetes PVCs from the operator's cluster). Per-sandbox volumes are unsupported: E2B volumeMounts refused 400 and volume endpoints 501 ('per-sandbox volumes').

volume_shared.note: An env's PVCs are mounted into every sandbox claimed from that env simultaneously; read-write sharing requires a ReadWriteMany storage class in the operator's cluster (not stated in docs). Derived from the env override semantics.
